topic: Why you can't tickle yourself: brain prediction of self-touch
hook: Your brain won't let you tickle yourself

slides.title: It predicts your touch
slides.body: Your brain forecasts what your own hand will feel and turns the sensation down before it even arrives.
slides.image_prompt: A single white feather floating above a glowing translucent brain model on a dark background, soft blue light
slides.credit: Joao Estevao Andrade de Freitas (Public domain) via wikimedia

slides.title: The cerebellum does it
slides.body: Brain scans at UCL showed the cerebellum flags self-made touch, so the brain's tickle response barely reacts.
slides.image_prompt: Anatomical model of a human brain with the cerebellum glowing amber, dark moody studio lighting

slides.title: A robot broke the trick
slides.body: When a robot delayed people's own strokes by 200 milliseconds, the touch started to feel ticklish again.
slides.image_prompt: A small robotic arm holding a soft feather in a dim laboratory, glowing timer light beside it
slides.credit: European Space Agency (CC BY-SA 3.0 igo) via wikimedia

slides.title: Why fights escalate
slides.body: Your own push feels weaker than one you receive, so in lab tests people hit back about 40% harder without noticing.
slides.image_prompt: Two red boxing gloves on a dark floor, one slightly bigger than the other, dramatic spotlight

slides.title: Rats laugh too
slides.body: Tickled rats make 50 kHz chirps, too high for us to hear, and chase the tickler for more.
slides.image_prompt: A cute brown rat on a soft blanket with faint glowing sound waves rising from it, warm light

cta: Follow for facts your brain hides
caption:
Try to tickle yourself right now. Nothing happens, because your brain predicts every move of your own fingers and mutes the feeling before it lands.

The same trick makes your own push feel weaker than someone else's. In a 2003 study in Science, people asked to match a push hit back about 40% harder each round without noticing. Sources: Blakemore et al. (UCL) and Shergill et al., Science.

Are you super ticklish, or totally immune? 👇
